claims.claim_text: Other than M4, all other models cause the agent to collide with the parked vehicle about half the time.
claims.normalized_text: All models except M4 cause about 50% collision rate with parked vehicle.

claims.claim_text: The baseline M0 model can also get stuck behind the parked vehicle in some of the scenarios.
claims.normalized_text: Baseline M0 model sometimes gets stuck behind parked vehicle.

claims.claim_text: The model M4 nudges around the parked vehicle and then brings the agent back to the lane center.
claims.normalized_text: Model M4 successfully nudges around parked vehicle and returns agent to lane center.

claims.claim_text: The model’s ability to learn to avoid collisions and nudge around objects is attributed to training with the collision loss and the trajectory perturbation.
claims.normalized_text: Training with collision loss and trajectory perturbation enables model to avoid collisions and nudge around objects.

claims.claim_text: Comparing model M3 and M4, "imitation dropout" was more effective at learning the right behavior than only re-weighting the imitation losses.
claims.normalized_text: Imitation dropout is more effective than re-weighting imitation losses for learning correct behavior.

claims.claim_text: In this scenario, several variations are generated by changing the starting speed of the agent relative to the parked car, creating situations of increasing difficulty.
claims.normalized_text: Varying agent starting speed relative to parked car creates increasing difficulty scenarios.

claims.claim_text: When the agent approaches the parked car at very high relative speed, it does not have enough time to nudge around the car given the dynamic constraints.
claims.normalized_text: High relative speed limits agent's ability to nudge around parked car due to dynamic constraints.
